_about: How each machine is wired as it leaves the factory, for the wiring map's Out of the box view (wiring_map.py). Each harness is traced from a drawing in the official Gaggiuino docs; colors are the ones that drawing labels, and the docs note that colors vary by year and model. Ends name map terminals: lamp and switch spades, boiler pins, the socket, pump, valve and earth spades, plus parts only the factory harness has: the brew thermostat (bt:a, bt:b), the steam thermostat (st:a, st:b) and the factory's crimp splices (J0, J1 and so on; the map picks the side). lab names the stock connector at each end where the stock wiring guide names one (Ba, Bb, Sa, Sb, Pb, B4, S4, S5, and on the Classic P1-2, 1, 2, 3, P3-4, F). sys: L line, H heater circuit, N neutral, E earth, LMP lamp lead. The Classic has no crimp splices: where two wires meet, they share a connector on one spade. missing: schematics with no factory drawing to trace, and the note shown instead.

junctions.J5: Factory splice: the elements' return to the steam thermostat

gc-120.noearth: Most 120 V Classics left the factory with no earth wire, so none is drawn. The drawing's green earth wires are the grounding retrofit.

cw-gcp-230.text: Out of the box isn't drawn for the 230 V Classic Pro: the official docs have no drawing of the plain 230 V Pro's stock wiring. Their archive has Gaggia's diagram of the 240 V Pro Eco, which adds a standby board.
